approvalTitle: tasks.md: converting the Ansible structure diagram (written against the recommended amendment)
content:
# Tasks Document

One Developer owns this specification, per CLAUDE.md's one-owner-per-specification rule, and works it in one worktree (`.claude/worktrees/ans`, branch `features/ansible-structure-disl-fbl`). **The order is the design's eleven steps and it is load-bearing**: the transcript is frozen before anything changes (task 1), derivation is switched while the reading stays as it is (tasks 5 and 6), the reading is switched under an unchanged derivation (tasks 7 and 8), and who watches the folder changes last (task 10), so that a difference in the transcript names one cause. The design's step 3 is two tasks here (3 and 4), because library work and a bundled definition are reviewed apart; every other task is one design step.

**Every task is one pull request into `develop` and leaves the four gates green.** No task is expected to change the transcript: Q2, Q3 and Q4 keep today's behaviour by default. A task whose transcript differs at all is not delivered.

**Tasks 2 and 12 have work in etalii-adp/etalii.adp**, through that repository's own pull requests: task 2 rewrites the definition and its companion there, and task 12 brings the companion to its final state there and offers the binding as an example.

**Which tasks wait, and on what:**

- **Task 4 waits on task 2 being merged in etalii.adp.** A definition is bundled from a merged commit and never from a branch.
- **Task 3 is delivered only after task 2 is merged**, because its list of missing constructs is taken from a load of the merged definition. Its items D1 to D3 are known already and may be worked while task 2 is in review.
- **Task 9 is shared library work that `helm-chart-disl-fbl` also needs** (the folder body read by a plugin). Whichever specification reaches it first delivers it, as a pull request that changes the library only. Before starting task 9, check `develop` for a folder body: where the other specification has delivered it, task 9 is reduced to adding what this tool still lacks, each part with its own test seen to fail first, and may be empty.
- **Task 10 waits on tasks 8 and 9.** The store and the watched folder leave the product code when the library's folder body watches, settles and reads again, and not before.
- **Task 11 touches no backend file** and may land at any time after task 4.
- **No task waits on a language change.** Each of the ten language gaps is stood in for by named module code (`AnsibleFolderListing`, `AnsibleInventoryRows`, `AnsibleFindings`, the reveal handler in `AnsibleCanvas.tsx`, `AnsibleLayout`) and reported. Removing a stand-in when etalii.adp changes a language is a later specification, and nobody starts it from this document.
- **The four behaviours of Q2, the repeated ids of Q3 and the seven quirks of Q4 are kept**, each visible in the transcript. Changing one is a later change of its own with a test seen to fail first, and is not a task here.

**This document is written against the recommended option of the amendment the design proposes; a ruling that differs is a small amendment to the tasks named.** The amendment gives Requirement 3.2 a clause that lets the sentence of `ansible.unreadable-yaml` be composed by the code that hands the findings to the host, and has Requirement 6.1 name that stand-in. It touches task 2 (the companion names the stand-in), task 6 (`AnsibleFindings` composes the sentence), task 8 (the list of what the module keeps) and task 12 (the table of remaining classes). Should the ruling be that the sentence becomes DISL's own, task 6 drops the composition and regenerates the transcript on purpose for that one sentence, and tasks 2, 8 and 12 drop the stand-in from their lists.

---

## The coverage diff, run before this document was raised

**44 acceptance criteria in the requirements; 44 claimed by the tasks below; none unclaimed, nothing claimed that is not a criterion, and none claimed twice.**

| Requirement | Criteria | Claimed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4 | 1 (1.1, 1.2, 1.3), 12 (1.4) |
| 2 | 5 | 2 (2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4), 4 (2.5) |
| 3 | 6 | 5 (3.1, 3.4, 3.6), 6 (3.2, 3.3), 8 (3.5) |
| 4 | 7 | 7 (4.1 to 4.7) |
| 5 | 4 | 7 (5.1), 10 (5.2, 5.3, 5.4) |
| 6 | 3 | 8 (6.1), 10 (6.2), 12 (6.3) |
| 7 | 4 | 11 (7.1 to 7.4) |
| 8 | 3 | 3 (8.2), 9 (8.1, 8.3) |
| 9 | 4 | 1 (9.4), 2 (9.1), 12 (9.2, 9.3) |
| 10 | 4 | 4 (10.3), 12 (10.1, 10.2, 10.4) |

Six criteria are worked in more than one task and claimed by the one that finishes them. Criterion 3.4's property refusal is stated once only from task 7, where it becomes the binding's `readOnly`; its tests and the reparenting sentence are task 5's. Criterion 3.5 holds for rows from task 5 and for findings from task 6, and is claimed by task 8, where the payloads come from the DISL model too. Criterion 3.6 is begun in task 5 with the provider's logic, and task 6 adds the rule set to the same oracle. Criterion 4.1's example is offered to etalii.adp in task 12, when the binding is final. Criterion 6.2 is begun in task 6 and claimed by task 10, where the store and the watched folder leave. Criterion 9.1 is claimed by task 2, which writes the ten gaps into the companion, and task 12 adds any gap the implementation found.

**The diff is run again at task 12**, traced to the tests, files and strings the work produced and not to a task's promise, and two traces are read back to their artefacts to check that the evidence is that criterion's and not a neighbour's.

---
